study.title: Unmanned aerial vehicle-based weed segmentation from multispectral imagery in an edge computing environment
study.short_title: PRC-Net lightweight: mIoU 0.840, Jetson TX2 17.05 FPS

segmentation.domain: Soil/crop/weed 3-class semantic segmentation of UAV multispectral imagery (sugar beet WeedMap RedEdge-M/Sequoia + sesame Sesame Aerial) for onboard weed mapping and site-specific/variable-rate treatments; explicitly designed for lightweight edge deployment (Jetson TX2, real-time requirement ~15+ FPS) with minority-class (weed) preservation under extreme class imbalance (IR up to 405.5)
segmentation.best_model: PRC-Net: 4-stage encoder-decoder with per-stage PRF modules (progressive receptive-field fusion: 1x1 -> 3x3 -> 5x5 convs with channel concatenation) + CSA modules (channel synergy-focused second-order attention: GAP/GMP + channel covariance/GCP + 1D-conv excitation) + LCFE bottleneck (parallel CCB atrous branch dilations 1/2/3 and LSFB depthwise-separable dense branch); best on all three datasets - RedEdge-M mIoU 0.8397 (Bg 0.9845/Crop 0.8321/Weed 0.7025, F1 0.8910), Sequoia mIoU 0.6520 (Weed 0.1863), Sesame Aerial mIoU 0.6961 (Weed 0.5144); 13.30 M params, 41.46 GFLOPs, 17.05 FPS on Jetson TX2

dataset.name: Public UAV-captured multispectral datasets only (no author collection): WeedMap (Sa et al. 2018) with two sub-datasets from sugar beet fields in Eschikon, Switzerland and Rheinbach, Germany - RedEdge-M (MicaSense RedEdge-M on DJI Inspire 2, 5 bands R/G/B/RE/NIR; official splits train subsets 000/001/002, test 003) and Sequoia (Parrot Sequoia on DJI Mavic, 4 bands R/G/RE/NIR; train 006/007, test 005); Sesame Aerial dataset (Imran Moazzam et al. 2022) - sesame fields, Agrocam NDVI on DJI Phantom 3 UAV, 3-band NGB composite, TIR-derived crop head detection with crop growth 16-45 days, diverse illumination/soil-moisture/mixed light-shadow conditions, 1200 train / 720 test images.
dataset.note: Patch count for Sesame Aerial explicitly given (1200 train + 720 test); WeedMap RedEdge-M/Sequoia splits are dataset-provider groups (000/001/002 train, 003 test; 006/007 train, 005 test) without per-split image counts in the text. Original patches 480x360 resized to 320x320; horizontal/vertical flip augmentation. Class imbalance (IR majority/minority, lower better): RedEdge-M train 29.26 / test 43.79; Sequoia train 405.54 / test 380.19 (extreme, weeds tiny fraction); Sesame Aerial train 6.57 / test 3.01.

segmentation.backbone: Custom lightweight encoder-decoder. Encoder: 4 stages, each = PRF module (progressive 1x1/3x3/5x5 conv receptive-field expansion with channel-wise input-concat at each convolution, pointwise dim-reduction) + CSA module (second-order channel attention: global average + global max pooling + CxC channel-covariance matrix compressed via 1D-conv+GAP1D, 1D-conv excitation + sigmoid) + ReLU + max pooling (halves resolution except final stage). Bottleneck LCFE: CCB = parallel atrous convs (dilation 1/2/3) + pointwise + CSA; LSFB = depthwise-separable convolutions in local dense connectivity + GeLU + transposed conv; CCB/LSFB outputs concatenated. Decoder: Conv2DB blocks (2 convs + ReLU + transposed conv) with encoder skip connections; softmax head. Kernel widths K in {24, 48, 128, 256}. Training: Adam (beta1 0.9/beta2 0.999), LR 1e-3 -> min 1e-6, batch 6 (RedEdge-M) / 12 (Sequoia) / 10 (Sesame), 150 epochs, early stopping; loss = categorical focal (gamma 2.0, alpha 0.25) + Dice, weighted lambda=0.7

mIoU.quote: PRC-Net is validated on the publicly available WeedMap (RedEdge-M, Sequoia) and Sesame Aerial datasets, achieving mean intersection over union (MIOU) values of 0.8397, 0.6520, and 0.6961, respectively
mIoU.ambiguity: Value = RedEdge-M (best dataset). Dataset-wise mIoU: RedEdge-M 0.8397 (Bg 0.9845/Crop 0.8321/Weed 0.7025); Sequoia 0.6520 (Bg 0.9804/Crop 0.7893/Weed 0.1863) under extreme weed class imbalance; Sesame Aerial 0.6961 (Bg 0.8702/Crop 0.7036/Weed 0.5144). All at 320x320 input.

mPA.ambiguity: Mean pixel accuracy not reported; per-class IoU, mIoU, Precision, Recall and F1 reported instead.

F1.ambiguity: Single overall F1 defined in the paper as harmonic mean of GLOBAL precision and recall (Eq. 36), i.e. 2PR/(P+R) with P 0.9239 / R 0.8603 = 0.891 on RedEdge-M, not a class-wise or mean-class F1. Dataset-wise F1: Sequoia 0.7011, Sesame Aerial 0.7082.

Dice.ambiguity: Dice used only as a training loss component (not an evaluation metric); IoU/F1 are the reported metrics.

weed_F1.ambiguity: Weed-class F1 not reported separately; weed-class IoU reported instead (0.7025 RedEdge-M, 0.1863 Sequoia, 0.5144 Sesame Aerial) and discussed in the F1-field ambiguity.

crop_F1.ambiguity: Crop-class F1 not reported separately; crop-class IoU reported (0.8321 RedEdge-M, 0.7893 Sequoia, 0.7036 Sesame Aerial).

edge.device: NVIDIA Jetson TX2 embedded module: Pascal-family GPU 256 CUDA cores, 8 GB shared memory, <7.5 W module spec - real edge-device deployment; measured 58.65 ms/image, 17.05 FPS, satisfying the reported real-time onboard-deployment requirement (Menshchikov threshold). Desktop reference: NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1070 8 GB, 10.53 ms, 94.97 FPS
edge.framework: Python 3.10.12, PyTorch 2.6.0 on Ubuntu 20.04 (Intel i7-3770K 4 cores, 32 GB RAM); inference timed on Jetson TX2

fps.quote: on the Jetson TX2 it requires 58.65 ms and achieves 17.05 FPS
fps.ambiguity: Measured on Jetson TX2 at 320x320 input. Desktop GTX 1070: 94.97 FPS. edge.reported=true (on-device embedded measurement).

latency_ms.quote: On the desktop system, PRC-Net requires 10.53 ms per image and achieves 94.97 FPS, whereas on the Jetson TX2 it requires 58.65 ms and achieves 17.05 FPS
latency_ms.ambiguity: Measured per-image inference latency on Jetson TX2 at 320x320 input; desktop GTX 1070 10.53 ms. edge.reported=true.

power_w.ambiguity: No power draw measured for the model; the <7.5 W figure is the Jetson TX2 MODULE specification, not an on-device power measurement. Model GPU memory footprint 0.58 GB (Table 12).

params_M.quote: the proposed model contains 13.30 M parameters, requires 0.58 GB of GPU memory, and incurs 41.46 GFLOPs
params_M.ambiguity: Structural efficiency figure at 320x320; reported alongside competing methods (e.g. SegFormer-B0 4.63 M, UNet-EfficientNetB0 10.82 M, TransUNet 105.12 M).

gflops.quote: requires 0.58 GB of GPU memory, and incurs 41.46 GFLOPs
gflops.ambiguity: GFLOPs at 320x320 input; lighter than SegNet 60.90, DeepLabv3 92.96, TransUNet 250.85; UNet-EfficientNetB0 28.09 and SegFormer-B0 22.55 are lighter but less accurate.

issues: edge.reported=true: real Jetson TX2 on-device measurements - 17.05 FPS / 58.65 ms at 320x320 (desktop GTX 1070: 94.97 FPS / 10.53 ms); params 13.30 M, gflops 41.46, GPU mem 0.58 GB. No precision (FP16/INT8) stated; power_w is device spec only (<7.5 W module), not measured.
Public datasets only (uav_collected=false): WeedMap sugar beet (RedEdge-M 5-band on DJI Inspire 2; Sequoia 4-band on DJI Mavic) + Sesame Aerial NGB on Phantom 3 + Agrocam NDVI (1200 train/720 test).

SOTA comparison retrained under unified protocol; PRC-Net best on all three datasets. Results vary strongly with class imbalance: weed IoU 0.7025 (RedEdge-M, IR~29-44) vs 0.1863 (Sequoia, IR~380-406) - authors attribute degradation to extreme minority-class scarcity, not architecture.
Loss ablation: CFL+Dice weighted combo (lambda=0.7) best (mIoU 0.8397 vs Dice-only 0.7865 / focal-only 0.8330). Full module ablation Table 2 (baseline U-Net 0.7791 -> proposed 0.8397).

Extensive SOTA table (14 models) and per-dataset comparisons in Tables 9-11; confusion matrices confirm crop-weed spectral similarity is the dominant error source. The reported overall F1 (0.8910 RedEdge-M) is the harmonic mean of global precision/recall, not class-wise.
